categories.name: Scale, layout and route readability
categories.evidence: The four corner cutaways and player-height views show a legible route from the arrival gate through scanner and cargo inspection, with yellow floor markings carrying the eye. C06_CART_GATE_G1 and PLAYER_REVERSE show the cart gate occupying much of the inspection opening; the split painted lanes and adjacent equipment make the exact walking/cart relationship less immediate than the route stripes suggest.

categories.name: Grounded stylized shape language and object-specific construction
categories.evidence: The door, trolley frame, rollers, electrical service piping and counter hardware have recognizable functional construction. However, the dominant scanner, cart gate, cargo tunnel, arrival door and wall structure rely on broad rectangular masses, repeated slab panels and near-identical heavy trim. C01_ENTRY, C02_HERO_DOCK, HERO_SCANNER and HERO_CARGO repeatedly read as box assemblies with detail added to their faces; the machinery lacks distinctive primary silhouettes and the architecture has little authored rhythm.

categories.name: Inspection/check-in hero hierarchy and functional composition
categories.evidence: The scanner arch and cargo examination tunnel dominate the intended process sequence, and C03_CHECKIN_COUNTER plus DETAIL_CHECKIN give the check-in hatch a clear working surface with paperwork and a stamp. The scanner and cart gate compete for the same visual center, while the hatch is visually isolated and its plain dark front carries little of the scene's strongest hierarchy. The inspection process is understandable, but its focal order is not yet decisive.

categories.name: Tactile material identity and UV/texture discipline
categories.evidence: Concrete-like floor, glazing, painted cabinets, exposed service metal and the fabric-like covered transfer trolley are distinguishable, with restrained surface noise. Across the broad wall, machine and cabinet faces, response remains mostly smooth and similar; painted steel, plastic housings and structural metal lack enough roughness and edge treatment variation to feel reliably tactile at room scale. HERO_UTILITIES, HERO_TROLLEY and HERO_CARGO show the strongest material separation; C01_ENTRY and C02_HERO_DOCK show the weaker dominant surfaces.

categories.name: Localized lighting, depth and bleak atmosphere without hiding geometry
categories.evidence: Warm practical pools at the check-in hatch, office and concealed support trolley create useful localized contrast, especially in C03_CHECKIN_COUNTER, C07_OFFICE_INTERIOR and C08_CONCEALED_SUPPORT_H1. Most circulation views remain broadly and evenly illuminated, while the heavy roof grid collapses to near-black across C01_ENTRY, C02_HERO_DOCK and C10_ROOF_SERVICES. Some secondary detail is lost in shadow, and the repeated cool fill leaves limited depth between major forms.

categories.name: Approved spawn colour coherence and restrained accents
categories.evidence: Muted walls, charcoal/navy structure and controlled hazard yellow with orange signage remain restrained and legible. Compared with the approved spawn references, the dock shifts toward blue cabinets and a cool gray field, with less of the warm rust/orange locker mass and warm institutional wall tone that anchor the reference. The accent scheme is functional, but the room's overall color relationship to the approved spawn is only partial.

categories.name: Purposeful worker traces and coercive institutional storytelling
categories.evidence: The covered transfer trolley and numbered custody label imply concealed handling; the check-in papers, stamp and counter setup imply daily procedure. WALL_OFFICE_FRONT places “WE VALUE YOUR TIME” above “ALL DELAYS ARE YOUR RESPONSIBILITY,” a strong coercive reinterpretation, and WALL_SOUTH shows a smaller “YOUR WORK MATTERS” poster. Yet most walls and inspection bays remain blank, worker-specific wear and personal traces are scarce, and the strongest story cues are small text panels rather than a broader arrangement of used objects.

gate_basis: The 7-category visual mean is far below the required 99 overall, and every independently scored visual category is below the strict >93 category gate. Category 8 is pending and cannot change the locked visual scores.
